purpose: The design and content-production suggestion layer: a paste-ready design prompt, design suggestions with live status, the article topic queue with published/pending status, organic-traffic tactics, editorial voice rules, and a decision register. Every row is a suggestion for the owner to review before anything is implemented. Facts about the current site carry source links; everything else is a recommendation, not a claim.
how_to_read: Status values describe the repository as built on 2026-11-16 and are checked against the files themselves: 'Implemented' means the generated pages already do this; 'Partial' means it exists but a named part is missing; 'Pending' means it has not been started. Decision rows are left blank on purpose — this page exists so a path can be chosen before work begins.
design_prompt:
ZONE1 KITCHEN — CURRENT DESIGN & EDITORIAL BRIEF (19 November 2026)

PURPOSE
A useful, polished kitchen buying publication, openly AI-assisted and documentation-based. Never disguise it as a human test lab. Three documented air-fryer formats are compared; five submitted links are recorded separately from the account holder's unconfirmed product intent. No conversion, ranking, profit or popularity result exists.

INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE
Reader navigation: Air fryers / Compare / The journal / Our approach / RSS. One Workspace group exposes every owner dashboard; repeat the complete index in the footer. The front page leads with the buyer's job and format choices, practical existing guides, a seasonal edit and a quiet method note. No dashboard metric wall or sidebar on the reader first screen.

VISUAL SYSTEM
Maintain publication/style.css and publication/app.js; build.py emits canonical assets unchanged. Warm paper, forest ink/green, terracotta and restrained serif headings with system-sans body/UI. Keep readable body copy, visible keyboard focus, responsive native details menus, independently scrollable source tables and reduced-motion support. Use 44px as the control-design preference, not a claim of WCAG conformance. WCAG 2.5.8 AA is 24px with exceptions/spacing; 2.5.5 AAA is 44px. Compact source chips have 24px targets. Test, do not assert accessibility from CSS alone.

DISCLOSURE & IMAGERY
The exact sentence 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.' sits in a visible strip BELOW the masthead and BEFORE main content, with a footer repetition. Keep material-connection information near the action. Product purchase buttons remain gated on documented intended listings and enrolled-Associates destination/report tests. Every Amazon product anchor, including citations, has rel=sponsored.
Generic AI-generated kitchen atmosphere is permitted only when labeled editorial illustration, not a product photograph or test scene. Format drawings are explicitly not to scale. No Amazon imagery is copied. Rights-cleared model photography is a separate unresolved route; never generate realistic product evidence or invent an owner licence.

EVIDENCE & VOICE
Every factual table row has official evidence; absent values are blank and flagged. A registered-host link proves traceability, not that a claim is true. Read the relevant passage. Attribute brand claims, dates and configuration. Retain conflicting source statements and publish corrections; never pick the more convenient passage of a safety manual. Do not invent product experience, an editor, credentials, customer testimonials or awards. Titles and target queries are editorial hypotheses until authorized reports supply demand evidence. Human-sounding means precise and helpful, not falsely human-authored.

MONEY & MEASUREMENT
Preserve all five exact supplied links. Intended ASIN/listing/date/source and observed redirects are separate. shopnow047c-20 is selected, not confirmed active or applied. A missing tag on a landing URL proves nothing about attribution. Do not manufacture replacement links from candidate ASINs.
No Amazon price, rating, availability or review data is displayed. §2(b) has specified Amazon-served/API price routes; this site has no authorized feed. No price alerts, scraping, fake clicks, revenue forecasts or training on restricted Program Content.
The single v2 contract is page_view, outbound_click, article_engagement (60 active seconds, not completion), comparison_interaction (product-guide activation, not table visibility), and operator-only affiliate_report_import. Production collection is off; local fixture tests are not hosting or attribution proof. No unique-session or reported-order figure is inferred from browser events. The campaign ledger remains empty without authorized reports.

SEARCH & CADENCE
Keep reader canonicals, truthful WebSite/Article/BreadcrumbList metadata, sitemap and RSS generated together. Owner/research pages are noindex,follow. scripts/stage_pages.py wraps historical deployment copies as noindex archives without rewriting their sources. No robots disallow that prevents crawlers reading noindex. Do not advance all source/article dates merely by rebuilding; record substantive corrections individually.
Review one buyer question each Tuesday from 24 November 2026, at most one source-approved guide. New writing is paused pending production measurement/access. Monthly query-led review needs actual Search Console/property access and authorized reports. No invented verification token, indexing promise, trend score or high-conversion label.

DECISIONS & ACCEPTANCE
Keep suggestions, questions and the decision brief reviewable. Actions under the standing autonomous/reversible policy go into decision-log.implemented, never owner choices[]. Account/privacy/rights/intent permissions cannot be inferred from silence.
Before merging: run scripts/ci-check.sh, the canonical pre-build hash check, Python/Node contract tests, staged-artifact archive checks and local HTTPS real-browser checks. Confirm keyboard/no-JS/print and narrow layouts. Then verify Actions and live Pages read-back. A passed build is not proof of legal compliance, semantic source adequacy, traffic or sales.

design.status_note: The generator and browser checks require this placement; it is not a legal-compliance certification.

design.suggestion: Product cards: verified specs only; blank cells stay blank with a flagged pill; each row links to its official source

design.suggestion: Comparison matrix: verified specs side by side, gaps visible, no price column
design.why: Program Policies restrict price display; showing gaps is honest and defensible.
design.path: compare.html stays a verified-only matrix with per-cell sources.

design.suggestion: Category subpages: one category index plus one page per product, with the category index growing as products are added

design.suggestion: Add JSON-LD (WebSite, Article, BreadcrumbList), Open Graph, Twitter card and meta descriptions to every page
design.why: Helps search engines understand the site and improves click-through from results and social shares.
design.path: Emit from build.py layout(); keep it static; guard it with a build check.
design.status_note: Shipped by pass 9 (PR #69) and extended by PR #74; enforced by build guard check_seo_metadata. Product/Offer/AggregateRating markup is deliberately not emitted because the site publishes no price or rating.

design.suggestion: Mobile-first: single-column stack below ~640px, readable touch targets, no horizontal scroll
design.why: Most affiliate traffic arrives on mobile.
design.path: Verify with device emulation before each release.
design.status_note: Real-browser reflow checks cover canonical pages at 320, 390, 768 and 1440px. Tables scroll independently; long badges and machine identifiers wrap.

design.suggestion: Accessibility: colour contrast >= 4.5:1, focus-visible outlines, alt text, semantic headings
design.why: Legal good practice; excludes no readers.
design.path: Audit the CSS variables against WCAG AA once per quarter.
design.status_note: Visible focus, alt text and semantic structure are implemented. Scoped axe checks found and prompted repairs to text-link cues and source-chip targets. No full WCAG conformance certificate is claimed.

design.suggestion: Magazine furniture on money pages: production-method byline, an 'in this guide' strip, and a visible freshness stamp
design.why: A reader deciding whether to trust a recommendation asks who wrote the page and when it was last checked. Both answers exist in the data layer today; neither is on the page a shopper lands on.
design.path: One byline line and one freshness stamp in the page templates; the strip is a short list of the page's own section headings. No new data required.
design.status_note: Articles now carry the truthful Zone1 Kitchen AI-assisted byline and recorded source-read dates; about.html explains the method. A named human editor and complete money-page furniture are not invented.

design.suggestion: Keep format choices and practical reading ahead of owner metrics
design.why: A buyer needs to see the goods before the paperwork. The tiles stay on the page, one screen later.
design.path: Editorial hero, three illustrated format cards, journal cards and separate owner brief.
design.status_note: Updated 19 November; no inline metric dashboard on the front page.

design.suggestion: Add the two merchandising rows — 'Best for' and 'Check first' — to the cards and the product pages
design.why: Those are the two questions a buyer asks in order, and both are answerable from rows this site already publishes.
design.path: One MERCH register in build.py, rendered by merch_pair(); cells cite the same source chips as the table below them.
design.status_note: Source-derived decision blocks remain on documented product pages. Home cards use a concise feature/trade-off and link to the guide; no purchase ranking is asserted.

design.suggestion: Show the brand's own list price, with the policy reason no Amazon price appears beside it
design.why: A shop without a price looks unlike a shop; an affiliate site without the reason looks like it is hiding something.
design.path: price_line() reads the registered brand list price and states that Program Policies 2(b) and 6(t) keep Amazon's figure off the page.
design.status_note: Brand list prices are dated historical snapshots, not current Amazon offers or proven MSRP. The policy note now states the permitted Amazon-served/API routes rather than a universal ban.

design.suggestion: Mobile-first type, preferred 44px controls, scrolling-table hints and comparison route
design.why: The comparison table is the site's product. On a phone it was the hardest thing to reach and the easiest thing to lose.
design.path: Clamp() per heading level, min-height on interactive chrome only, a bottom-anchored bar on reader surfaces, and a JS-revealed hint that appears only when a table is genuinely clipped.
design.status_note: 44px is the preferred control design target; compact source chips use 24px. W3C AA minimum and AAA enhanced criteria are separately sourced, including exceptions. Native menus work without JS; no conformance claim.

voice_rules.rule: One topic per page, and every page stamps when its sources were read
voice_rules.why: Focus for the reader, freshness signal for search engines, and an honest record of what the page is based on.

voice_rules.rule: Human voice: contractions, questions, specific numbers instead of 'very/really/incredible', short and long sentences mixed
voice_rules.why: The single fastest way to stop reading like generated filler. Specifics are also the only thing this site has - every number is sourced.

voice_rules.rule: Label vendor claims: anything the manufacturer says about its own product is marked a brand claim, not a tested fact
voice_rules.why: A repeated brand claim presented as an finding is the classic fake-review pattern; labelling it is both honest and compliant.

voice_rules.rule: Working titles are questions or decisions a reader types - never announcements like 'The Ultimate Guide to...'
voice_rules.why: Announcement titles are the loudest AI-slop tell, and they match no search query anyone types.

voice_rules.rule: Headlines name the thing and the payoff; no curiosity-gap clickbait
voice_rules.why: A reader arriving from search must know in one second what the page does for them. Curiosity gaps earn clicks and lose trust, and trust is this site's only product.

voice_rules.rule: Numbers in headlines only when the page sources them in the body
voice_rules.why: A headline number is a promise the body has to keep; an unsourced one is the slop tell readers notice first.

voice_rules.rule: Seasonal pages carry their year and their expiry, and never a countdown
voice_rules.why: Seasonal content must age honestly. Countdown timers are urgency theatre and contradict the site's deliberate no-Amazon-prices rule (Program Policies 2(b)).

voice_rules.rule: A product page may say what a machine is for and what to check before buying. It may not say what it is like to live with.
voice_rules.why: The first is a reading of published documents; the second is an experience nobody here has had, and FTC guidance makes having used the product the test for describing it.

voice_rules.rule: A price on this site is a brand's own list price, labelled as such, with the reason Amazon's figure is absent in the same breath.
voice_rules.why: Silence about price reads as an omission; an unlabelled price reads as today's price. Naming both the figure and the policy that keeps the other one off the page is the version a reader can check.
